format: the video's fundamental structure — exactly one):
presenter_age_band: visual estimate of the main presenter): late-teens-20s | 30s | 40s-plus | mixed | none
presenter_skin_tone: the main presenter's apparent skin tone, as a CASTING/REPRESENTATION attribute — banded on the Monk Skin Tone scale so the label is reproducible; report what is visible on screen, and note in evidence when lighting, filters, or colour grading make it uncertain). The value must be EXACTLY ONE of thes
presenter_attire: the main presenter's clothing register — a casting/styling choice this category uses deliberately): western-casual | ethnic-saree | ethnic-kurta-salwar | ethnic-other | professional-formal | sleepwear-homewear | uniform-occupational | unclear | none
presenter_hair: the main presenter's visible hair styling): long-open | long-tied | short | braided | covered | unclear | none
addressed_viewer: WHO the ad speaks to, judged from grammatical gender, pronouns, terms of address and the situation described — this category targets its viewer explicitly and the choice is a real variable): male-viewer | female-viewer | unspecified | unclear
address_mode: how the presenter relates to the viewer — exactly one): first-person-invitation (offers THEMSELVES as the person to talk to: "call me", "I'm waiting") | app-endorsement (describes the app and its users in third person) | testimonial-experience (narrates their own use: "I've been using this for month
regional_anchor: whether and how the ad signals a SPECIFIC place, region or local culture beyond merely being in a language — dress, dialect or slang, named place, local food, festival, landmark. This is a deliberate lever in this category): named-place (a city, state or region is named aloud or on screen) | dialect
setting: where the video takes place; for a simulated call, describe the MAIN presenter's visible background): bedroom | living-room | kitchen | balcony-outdoor-home | office-workplace | classroom | vehicle | street-outdoor | plain-studio | app-screen-only | multiple | unclear
language_spoken: the language actually spoken in audio): hindi | tamil | telugu | kannada | malayalam | bengali | marathi | gujarati | odia | punjabi | english | hinglish | none-music-only | (other — name it
subtitle_script: how burned-in captions are written — a testable creative choice, separate from which language): native-script | romanized (the language written in latin letters) | english | mixed | none
audio_mode: how the soundtrack is built — exactly one): presenter-sync-sound (speaks on camera, lips visible in sync) | voiceover (narration over footage, speaker not lip-synced) | dialogue (two or more speakers) | music-only (no speech at all) | ai-synthetic-voice (speech that is audibly synthesised or dubbed
call_modality: what kind of contact the ad actually promises — exactly one, the PRIMARY one): audio-call | video-call | chat-messaging | mixed | unspecified
hook: EXACTLY ONE — the attention device of the FIRST 3 SECONDS; put the verbatim opening line/text with translation and timing in evidence):
hook_verbal_line: the FIRST thing said aloud in the first 3 seconds — value is a SHORT English paraphrase of that line, lowercase, 3-8 words; evidence = the verbatim original-language line + English translation + timing. If nothing is spoken in the first 3 seconds, value "none" and say what plays instead in evidence
hook_visual: what is physically on screen during the first 3 seconds — exactly one): face-close-up | full-body | phone-screen (a phone or screen recording dominates) | call-ui (call interface chrome is the first thing seen) | text-card | scene (room/activity establishing shot) | split-screen
hook_presenter_action: what the main presenter is DOING in the first 3 seconds — exactly one): talking | waving-greeting | answering-call | doing-chore | lying-in-bed | dancing | applying-makeup-grooming | holding-phone | none (no presenter visible in the first 3 seconds
hook_emotion: the emotion the presenter PERFORMS in the first 3 seconds — exactly one; judge from face, voice and words, evidence says which): playful | flirtatious | confident | reassuring | urgent | shy | excited | sad-lonely | teasing | neutral | none (no presenter). These are the ONLY allowed values — never w
production_style: raw-ugc (handheld, natural light, deliberately amateur) | polished-ugc (creator format but visibly produced: stable frame, good light) | staged-professional (set design, professional grade) | ai-generated-look (visibly synthetic: AI face, uncanny motion, dubbed lip-sync, or a carried AI label
ai_content_label: yes (a visible "AI Generated Content" / "AI-Generated" tag appears) | no
app_ui_shown: whether the actual product interface appears at all — a real creative choice in this category, where many ads never show the app): none (no interface at any point) | end-card-only (interface or store badge appears only in the closing frame) | brief-glimpse | demo-throughout
scene_description: a 2-4 sentence factual description of what happens in the video from start to end — who, where, what they do, what changes; this is the human-readable context every later analysis reads alongside the facets. Put the full description in the value field; leave evidence as an empty string for this face
value_prop: one observation per DISTINCT selling point communicated — spoken, subtitled or shown. value is the proposition compressed to a 2-6 WORD LABEL, never a sentence and never an abstract category: "no fake profiles", "girls waiting to talk", "talk in your language". The full line, its translation and tim
price_point: the price the ad states — value is ALWAYS the currency symbol immediately followed by the number and nothing else ("₹1", "₹5", "₹49"), never words and never a unit phrase, so prices group and sort; evidence carries the verbatim line, what the price buys, and timing. Omit when no price is stated
price_metaphor: a colloquial cheapness comparison used to make the price feel small — comparing the cost to an everyday item or snack. Value is the concrete comparison; the verbatim line, translation and timing go in evidence
privacy_claim: one per DISTINCT privacy, anonymity or safety assurance made — value is the TYPE of assurance from this list, so that the same promise phrased three ways still groups; the verbatim line + translation + timing go in evidence): no-phone-number | no-real-name | identity-hidden | call-is-private | no-ju
persona_archetype: the IDENTIFIABLE ROLE the presenter plays — a character with an occupation or life-situation the video establishes through setting, activity or dialogue. Emit ONLY when a genuine role is identifiable; NEVER emit generic values like "young-woman" — gender and age are already core facets. Omit entirel
emotional_driver: the viewer NEED the ad speaks to — AT MOST TWO; put the exact line that reveals it in evidence): loneliness-companionship | boredom-timepass | shyness-social-anxiety | heartbreak-moving-on | flirtation-romance | stress-relief-unburdening | homesickness-distance | curiosity-novelty | affordability |
emotional_register: AT MOST TWO — the dominant emotional tones): playful | flirtatious | teasing | reassuring | sincere | energetic | confident | melancholic | conspiratorial
ad_objective_type: which side of the marketplace this ad recruits, when the ad makes it clear): user-acquisition (invites the viewer to install and TALK to people) | earner-recruitment (invites the viewer to install and EARN by taking calls) | unclear
cta: each distinct call-to-action — value is the TYPE of ask, from this list; the exact wording, where it appears (spoken, subtitle, on-screen badge, end-card) and its timing all go in evidence): download-install (download / install / get the app) | open-app (open or go into the app) | call-now (place a
store_badge: which app-store badge is shown, when one is): google-play | app-store | both | none
end_card_element: one observation per DISTINCT element present in the closing frame — use these exact labels, one observation each; evidence describes the element and gives timing. Omit the facet entirely when there is no distinct closing frame): logo | app-name | tagline | download-button | store-badge | price-super
social_proof: any user count, rating, popularity or endorsement claim — value is the TYPE as a short label; the verbatim claim goes in evidence
offer: any ACTUAL incentive — free trial, free minutes, bonus coins, discount. A price alone is NOT an offer, that is price_point; a cheapness comparison is price_metaphor
app_feature_named: one per DISTINCT product feature the ad names or shows — matching, filters, language choice, gifting, wallet, verification badge and so on, in the ad's own words
subtitle_style: the visual design of captions — describe as colour + shape, e.g. "yellow highlight bar", "white bold outline", "black bar white text"
secondary_content: a SECOND, unrelated content strip sharing the frame with the presenter — usually the top or bottom half — whose only job is holding attention: mobile-game gameplay, ASMR or satisfying clips, cooking b-roll and similar. Value is the concrete content type; evidence says where on screen, when, and what
pacing: overall edit rhythm): slow-single-take | moderate | fast-cut | rapid-montage
sound_dependency: whether the ad still communicates with sound OFF — judge from burned-in text and visual storytelling): works-muted (all key messages are on screen) | partially-dependent | sound-essential (key claims exist only in audio
brand_first_appearance_seconds: the timestamp in SECONDS when the advertised app — name, logo or pack — is first identifiable; value is the number alone, e.g. "3.5"; evidence says how it appears
price_first_mention_seconds: the timestamp in SECONDS when a price is first stated or shown; value is the number alone; "none" when no price appears
cta_timing_seconds: the timestamp in SECONDS when the call-to-action first appears, spoken or on screen; value is the number alone; "none" when there is no CTA
notable_device: ESCAPE HATCH — any prominent, deliberate creative device in this video that NONE of the facets above asks about: a split screen, a picture-in-picture, a countdown, a trend audio, a text-message overlay, a green screen, a reaction format, a POV framing, a meme format, anything an analyst would point
